model_and_data: Minimum ℓ2-norm (“ridgeless”) interpolation in high-dimensional least squares. The quoted data display is line-broken: it shows (xi, ϵi) ∼ Px × Pϵ and a response line that stops at “yi = xT”, then states E(xi) = 0, Cov(xi) = Σ, E(ϵi) = 0, and Var(ϵi) = σ2. One quoted feature map is xi = Σ1/2zi with zi a vector of i.i.d. entries, zi ∈Rp. Another quoted map is a one-layer neural network xi = ϕ(Wzi), with zi ∈Rd and W ∈Rp×d a matrix of i.i.d. entries; the activation clause continues past that line and is not completed here. The broken response display is not rewritten.
loss: The quoted object is the out-of-sample prediction risk of an estimator built from the training pair (X, y). A later quoted line says that risk has a bias-variance decomposition. The displayed formula for that risk is not one of the intact quoted lines, so it is not reconstructed. The estimator quote is the minimum ℓ2-norm least squares estimator of y on X.
varied_axis: Figure 1 is quoted as asymptotic risk curves against the limiting aspect ratio γ. The extract defines γ := p/n ∈(0, ∞), calls γ < 1 underparametrized and γ > 1 overparametrized, and also considers p and n diverging with p/n →γ. A separate caption line places min-norm least squares in the isotropic well-specified model at SNR = 1 and SNR = 5; those are different curves, not the same axis as γ. A quoted finite-sample line uses n = 200 and p = [γn], and that line stops at “across”.
held_fixed_axes: The quoted asymptotic scenario sends p and n to infinity with p/n →γ. Theorem 1, in the quoted lines, assumes i.i.d. feature entries with zero mean and unit variance and a finite moment of order 4 + η. The coefficient-norm display in that quote is broken: it ends at ∥β∥2 and the next line begins “2 = r2 for all n, p”; that display is not rewritten. A later single line sets SNR = r2/σ2. The quoted finite-sample markers use n = 200 and p = [γn]. SNR is not held fixed across the quoted Figure 1 curves, which name SNR = 1 and SNR = 5.
interpolation_definition: The extract defines interpolators as estimators that achieve zero training error. The min-norm estimator is the minimum ℓ2-norm least squares estimator of y on X, written ˆβ = (XT X)+XT y, where (XT X)+ is the pseudoinverse. The quoted ridgeless name is the limit ˆβ = limλ→0+ ˆβλ. The quoted ridge closed form is ˆβλ = (XT X + nλI)−1XT y. When X has full column rank, the quote reduces the min-norm estimator to ˆβ = (XT X)−1XT y; when X has rank n, the same quote says this estimator interpolates the training data. Gradient descent is quoted as initialized at β(0) = 0 on the least squares loss; under the quoted step-size bound, limk→∞β(k) = ˆβ, and the next line calls that the min-norm least squares solution.
assumptions: Interpolators are estimators that achieve zero training error.
A quoted feature map is xi = Σ1/2zi with zi a vector of i.i.d. entries and zi ∈Rp.
A quoted feature map is a one-layer neural network xi = ϕ(Wzi), with zi ∈Rd and W ∈Rp×d a matrix of i.i.d. entries.
The quoted data display states E(xi) = 0, Cov(xi) = Σ, E(ϵi) = 0, and Var(ϵi) = σ2. Its response line is broken after “yi = xT”.
The quote sets γ := p/n ∈(0, ∞), calls γ < 1 underparametrized, and calls γ > 1 overparametrized.
Proposition 2 assumes x ∼Px has the form x = Σ1/2z, where z has i.i.d. entries with zero mean, unit variance, and a finite 4th moment.
Theorem 1 assumes x ∼Px has i.i.d. entries with zero mean and unit variance.
The following quoted lines assume a finite moment of order 4 + η, for some η > 0, and the next line begins “2 = r2 for all n, p”.
When X has rank n, the quoted text says this estimator interpolates the training data.
Under the quoted step-size bound, limk→∞β(k) = ˆβ, and the next line of that quote calls it the min-norm least squares solution.
The quoted line sets SNR = r2/σ2.
result_type: Both a finite-n approximation and an asymptotic limit, together with finite-sample risk points. Theorems 2 and 5 are quoted as applying in a non-asymptotic setting where n and p are finite, and as providing a deterministic approximation of the risk with error bounds uniform in the distribution of the data. Another quoted line is the asymptotic scenario in which p and n diverge with p/n →γ. Figure 1 is quoted as plotting asymptotic risk curves, with finite-sample risks at n = 200 and p = [γn]. The formal verification quoted here is for least squares regression. For that least-squares risk, the extract says the second descent past the interpolation boundary (γ = 1) is explained by the variance decreasing as γ grows. That sentence is kept inside this least-squares setting.
transfer_limits: The quoted neural-network correspondence holds only in a lazy-training regime in which network weights do not change much during training. The following quoted lines say that, in a neural network, the feature representation and the regression function or classifier are learned simultaneously, and that in both the linear and nonlinear model settings the features X are not learned, but observed. The extract says learning X could change some aspects of interpolator behavior. The formal double-descent verification quoted here is least squares regression. Neural networks and random forests appear in a sentence that attributes an empirical trend to Belkin et al. The extract does not locate gradient-boosted trees or an essay corpus, and it does not locate a trained multilayer perceptron outside that lazy-training qualification.
